NEWLANDS: End of an era for SA oldest rugby stadium

By: Liz Fish | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

Unique Selling Point:
It’s the end of an era for Western Province Rugby fans and players alike- the grand old lady will be retired- after three years of negotiations Western Province Rugby Union has finally announced they are moving to Cape Town Stadium as the anchor tenant with 99 year lease. The first Super Rugby series to be played there in 2021. 2020 will be DHL Stormers last year at Newlands Stadium. That’s the end of a 128 years of fine rugby. The City of Cape Town will retain responsibility for repairs and maintenance and the operational costs of Cape Town Stadium. It will remain a multipurpose entity, with Western Province Rugby leasing the Cape Town Stadium for matches

Summary:
It’s been on the cards since 2012 but remains an emotional issue for many old timers. ”Save Newlands Stadium” a group of diehards are desperately fighting back trying to save the oldest rugby stadium in South Africa and the fourth-oldest rugby stadium in the world. The first-ever Springbok Test series against a touring British team was played in 1891. Newlands used to be regarded as one of the best rugby grounds in the world, combining intimate seating, a beautiful view of Table Mountain, and a great atmosphere. But it’s history is not entirely rosy. During Apartheid the Coloured fans were squashed into what used to be known as the Malay stands, later the South stand, squashed behind the goal posts. SACOS boycotted Newlands stadium for many years only returning after 1994.
Newlands stadium doesn’t meet the fire and safety standards of modern stadiums, the stands, field and scoreboard all need upgrading and to the WPRU just does not have the finances to upgrade the grand old lady. The WPRU has been in dire financial straits for many years now- current debt could be as high R53-million after interest payments were not settled with Remgro.


Further information:
WP Rugby’s business arm was placed into final liquidation by the Western Cape High court in 2016 after the union was slapped with an R276-million lawsuit by Aerios for reneging on an advertising rights contract with the company, that law suit is on-going. WPRU was one of the most profitable rugby unions but years of mismanagement have got them into the terrible financial crisis along with many corporate suite holders pulled out and dwindling numbers at the gates with DHL Stormers performance being in the doldrums.
Remgro stepped in with a R40 Million bail out to assist with paying salaries and contracting players but after they were unhappy with the deal and pulled out. Now WPRU debt to Remgro is R53 million and rising. WPRU has the biggest budget of all the South African rugby franchises spending R78 Million on 128 contract players in 2018. They have been threatened with lawsuits for loss of security of contracts from some players who could have taken on lucrative overseas deals
Investec Development Group were on board to develop Newlands site once WPRU vacates the stadium in 2021, and WPRFU would be 5% of the profits but carry none of the development costs. Zelt Marais pulled out of the deal at the 11th hour and went with a small developer with Flyt Property Investment (Dream World Investments 401 loan deal, Dream World part of Flyt) to pay R110-million to settle WPRFU debt to Remgro and Investec. CEO Paul Zacks resigned in January after spending years putting of work into the Investec deal. Although the new deal sounds good where WPRFU get a significant share of the profits the new agreement saw them sign away the rights to both Newlands and Brookside- extremely valuable real estate. This deal sees them carry 50% of development costs of Newlands.But WPRFU is in no financial position to fund any development so they stand to lose everything and they paid R2 million to broker the deal

Currently the professional wing of WPRFU has no CEO after Paul Zacks resigned and is being run by committee. This new deal could see WPRFU lose everything.

WPRFU will have a 99 year lease at Cape Town Stadium. Some fans say CT stadium was built for soccer and don't like the sloping stands but the facilities of a modern stadium with easy crowd access and transport outweighs the drawbacks. The pressure to move to a modern stadium has come from the South African Rugby Union who is reluctant to play test matches at Newlands and have held the Springbok practices and board meetings at the Cape Town stadium. In February 2019 they hosted the Super Heroes rugby game in the CT stadium with great success. DHL Stormers and WP Rugby will remain at Newlands for one last season but under Covid they could be playing to empty stands.

Script:


Link: This is a hallowed space for Western Province – and South African - rugby fans, you can feel the history in this place, the ghosts of so many rugby highlights as far back as 1891 when the 1st ever Springbok Test series was played here against the touring British team
Script: 130 years of rugby at Newlands, and everyone has a cherished memory, a special hero, or seminal game. But it’s ageing, the upkeep is prohibitively high, and it’s not up to international safety standards. Fan numbers and executive suites have dwindled, and Western Province Rugby Football Union who owns the stadium is in a financial crisis.
Link: Negotiations have been going on with the City of Cape Town for the past four years, to make Western Province Rugby Union the anchor tenant at Cape Town Stadium and the City would carry the costs for the upkeep and maintenance
Script: Although the die-hards can't contemplate the idea of moving, Stormers head coach John Dobson says the team has practiced there in the last few weeks, and he can see the upsides
John: Look physically it's just a magnificent stadium. It doesn't feel too open. You still feel like the people with the other people and the facilities are incredible and we are aware that the after match and the pre match and all that will be better there
Script: And former springboks like Jean De Villiers admits Newlands change rooms aren’t up to scratch
Jean “In terms of world standards it's uh it's probably not ideal to to have to have just two toilets and a team of 25 plus management and all of that to share pre game. You know it becomes quite tricky at times

Script: But, he is still heartbroken about the move
Jean: It is it is literally where I fell in love with rugby.I played my hundred year first Test match and I was able to run out onto the field with my kids with my family being here and my wife being pregnant with our son. My parents used to have season tickets was really like everything that I love about life and sport all thrown together
Mac All put together in this box right
Jean In this place

Script: Equally nostalgic, Goosain Abrahams has been coming here since he was 10

Goosain: I was here at my first test in 1958 Mac: 1958! Goosain South Africa and France score was three all, a drop goal by Pierre Delos and a try by ???? in the corner …..Then the Lions came here in 1962 I think then Cornet Wallet and his team came here

Script: Breyton Paulse’s speed and tries are legendary!
Breyton: there's one try that I scored against the Auckland Blues back in the day. It was a star studded Auckland Blues side where you know they had the likes of Carlos Spencer. Jono Lomu, Tana Umaga, those kind of players.

Mac: Oh yes.

Breyton a tri and ultimately that was a try that sort of won the game for us.

Script: So many legends - Morne Du Plessis, Schalk Burger, Chester Williams, Bobby Skinstad, Brian Habana, HO de Villiers, Percy Montgomery - the list goes on and on, and groundsman Mervyn Gabone has looked after most of them

Mervyn “Come out I say come on men come on

Script. As groundsman for the past 33 years he’s witnessed rugby transform firsthand, encouraging young black players like Siya Kolisi, who calls him papa, to push hard

Mac” What was it like to see him lifting the world cup

Mervyn Wow it was incredible it was huge for me I watched him come through and when he became captain it was good

Script: Newlands is all about the people, from the groundsman to the coach, traditions passed from one generation to the next. John Dobson’s father Paul, never missed a game from 1949, involved in all aspects of refereeing for over 60 years, he was your man if you wanted to know anything about Newlands. Sadly, he died of Covid in March.

Mac: Coach I also firstly want to send out condolences to your dad….. We're hoping that you're gonna have this conversation with him before you right.

John: He would be much better at it than me. Yeah. Thanks I appreciate it.

Mac: you speak about your dad and you say you know from 1949 he was here and I'm sure at some stage he was holding your hand as well.

John : The British and Irish Lions of 1974 was the first time I came here I was a ball boy once when I was 12. ….. I took Naas Botha sand in a bucket. You're playing against the British Lions in 1980. And I gave him the sand and he even said thank you

Script: But Newlands, like South Africa, had its dark days, Goosain stayed away from Newlands from 1962, only returning in 1995 - no normal sport in an abnormal society

Goosain: when I got to high school I realised that there was no ways I was going to sit in a segregated stands, this was by the way called the Malay stand. We were hemmed in here students were never allowed to sit on the field, that was reserved for the boys from the leafy suburbs …. but for us like for us we have to be behind the fence.

Script: Winning the World Cup in 1995 was the turning point in rugby that united the nation

Breyton: when you run out in a tunnel and people are going bonkers

Mac: you know when you hear that WP

Breyton: WP jou lekker ding … I've never experienced such wonderful fans the little sayings that they have in the shouting for the team no matter what ……some of them you know can barely you know sort of buy a ticket

Jean: we had four guys four five guys that used to come, ..I think they were given tickets eventually by the Union and their job was just to chirp every single opposing player that comes onto this field.

Goosain: even in the bad old days ….. what happens outside it was different but inside Newlands they were one homogenous supportive group

Script: Often called the 16th player, the legendary Newlands roar would carry Western Province over the line. Sadly, fans have dwindled and nostalgia isn’t enough to save Newlands from the wrecking ball

Link: Newlands sits on some of the most commercially valuable real estate in Africa, but exactly how it is to be re-developed remains under wraps. It will have to be rezoned by the City of Cape Town, but the talk is will be a mix of residential and commercial properties
Script: But the deals keep stalling, the amateur clubs control the professional body and the rescue deals the professional board negotiates, keep getting overruled. As things stand, nobody knows if this really is the last curtain for Newlands

Link: Western Province Rugby has been in financial trouble for a number of years with deals on and off the table. We asked President of the Union Zelt Marais for an interview, but he declined, saying things were still in process.
Mac: Is the move definitely happening for 2021, and does that mean all games will then be played there and this old lady goes goes to bed.

John: Yeah. You'd have to ask people several levels above my pay grade. I mean we're hearing talk but maybe not, but the plan is we're going to Greenpoint next year

Script: There have been 5 resignations from the professional board this year alone, and veteran sports journalist Rob Houwing says the boardroom battles and financial instability, is crippling
Rob: there's been really unacceptable level of instability in the last couple of years. You know the players haven't been sure ...where their next payday is gonna be coming from. 07:03:05:01
Mac: It's been I mean three deals in three years. It was the Remgro group then it was Investec. Now the Flight group but it still seems there's no money in the bag and there's no momentum.
Rob: You know that there's been a little bit of an ideological shift at a Newlands as well and it's a reflection of the sort of the changing times changing demographics and in South Africa the people who now wield the power have been wanting rightly or wrongly to sort of shift away from what what what might be called the sort of the old money and whether sort of doing a U-turn and seeking other sort of equity possibilities from corporations that don't have a massive sort of long standing reputation there are risks involved
Script: The rugby fraternity is now impatient for answers

Breyton. “ I never I never really thought in my wildest dreams when we were playing rugby that Newlands one day wouldn't be no more.

Script: Covid has already silenced the legendary Newlands roar, but they’re hoping they can lift the eerie silence just once more

Mac: What for you would be that ideal send off for your boys for your team and you know in memory, for people like your dad.

John: Siya Kolisi lifting the Currie Cup in front of a full Newlands on the 23th of January I could think of nothing more beautiful to say on lots of levels to say goodbye to Newlands

metadata.Unique Selling Point: It’s the end of an era for Western Province Rugby fans and players alike- the grand old lady will be retired- after three years of negotiations Western Province Rugby Union has finally announced they are moving to Cape Town Stadium as the anchor tenant with 99 year lease. The first Super Rugby series to be played there in 2021. 2020 will be DHL Stormers last year at Newlands Stadium. That’s the end of a 128 years of fine rugby. The City of Cape Town will retain responsibility for repairs and maintenance and the operational costs of Cape Town Stadium. It will remain a multipurpose entity, with Western Province Rugby leasing the Cape Town Stadium for matches
metadata.Summary: It’s been on the cards since 2012 but remains an emotional issue for many old timers. ”Save Newlands Stadium” a group of diehards are desperately fighting back trying to save the oldest rugby stadium in South Africa and the fourth-oldest rugby stadium in the world. The first-ever Springbok Test series against a touring British team was played in 1891. Newlands used to be regarded as one of the best rugby grounds in the world, combining intimate seating, a beautiful view of Table Mountain, and a great atmosphere. But it’s history is not entirely rosy. During Apartheid the Coloured fans were squashed into what used to be known as the Malay stands, later the South stand, squashed behind the goal posts. SACOS boycotted Newlands stadium for many years only returning after 1994. Newlands stadium doesn’t meet the fire and safety standards of modern stadiums, the stands, field and scoreboard all need upgrading and to the WPRU just does not have the finances to upgrade the grand old lady. The WPRU has been in dire financial straits for many years now- current debt could be as high R53-million after interest payments were not settled with Remgro.
metadata.Further information: WP Rugby’s business arm was placed into final liquidation by the Western Cape High court in 2016 after the union was slapped with an R276-million lawsuit by Aerios for reneging on an advertising rights contract with the company, that law suit is on-going. WPRU was one of the most profitable rugby unions but years of mismanagement have got them into the terrible financial crisis along with many corporate suite holders pulled out and dwindling numbers at the gates with DHL Stormers performance being in the doldrums. Remgro stepped in with a R40 Million bail out to assist with paying salaries and contracting players but after they were unhappy with the deal and pulled out. Now WPRU debt to Remgro is R53 million and rising. WPRU has the biggest budget of all the South African rugby franchises spending R78 Million on 128 contract players in 2018. They have been threatened with lawsuits for loss of security of contracts from some players who could have taken on lucrative overseas deals Investec Development Group were on board to develop Newlands site once WPRU vacates the stadium in 2021, and WPRFU would be 5% of the profits but carry none of the development costs. Zelt Marais pulled out of the deal at the 11th hour and went with a small developer with Flyt Property Investment (Dream World Investments 401 loan deal, Dream World part of Flyt) to pay R110-million to settle WPRFU debt to Remgro and Investec. CEO Paul Zacks resigned in January after spending years putting of work into the Investec deal. Although the new deal sounds good where WPRFU get a significant share of the profits the new agreement saw them sign away the rights to both Newlands and Brookside- extremely valuable real estate. This deal sees them carry 50% of development costs of Newlands.But WPRFU is in no financial position to fund any development so they stand to lose everything and they paid R2 million to broker the deal Currently the professional wing of WPRFU has no CEO after Paul Zacks resigned and is being run by committee. This new deal could see WPRFU lose everything. WPRFU will have a 99 year lease at Cape Town Stadium. Some fans say CT stadium was built for soccer and don't like the sloping stands but the facilities of a modern stadium with easy crowd access and transport outweighs the drawbacks. The pressure to move to a modern stadium has come from the South African Rugby Union who is reluctant to play test matches at Newlands and have held the Springbok practices and board meetings at the Cape Town stadium. In February 2019 they hosted the Super Heroes rugby game in the CT stadium with great success. DHL Stormers and WP Rugby will remain at Newlands for one last season but under Covid they could be playing to empty stands.
